source.title: Bug: Wait node with "Respond When: Form Is Submitted" delays the response until downstream nodes finish

source.body:
### Bug Description

The Wait node does not seem to respond to a form submission immediately when the Respond When option is set to Form Is Submitted.

The behavior appears to depend on whether the Wait node has downstream nodes connected to it. If there are no downstream nodes, the form response is sent immediately. However, if the workflow continues through additional nodes, including another Wait node, the form response is delayed until the downstream execution finishes.

This behavior does not seem consistent with the documented purpose of the Form Is Submitted option.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Wait node configured to wait for a form submission.
2. Set Respond When to Form Is Submitted.
3. Submit the form without connecting any downstream nodes to the Wait node.
4. Observe that the form responds immediately.
5. Now connect the first Wait node to several additional nodes, including a second Wait node.
6. Configure the second Wait node to wait for another event or form submission.
7. Submit the form again at the first Wait node.
8. Observe that the response is not sent immediately. Instead, it appears to wait until the downstream nodes finish executing, including the second Wait node.

### Expected behavior

When Respond When is set to Form Is Submitted, the form response should be sent immediately after the form is submitted, regardless of whether downstream nodes continue executing.

UPD: Generally there is no way to put 2 or more WAIT nodes in a row, no matter how additional nodes are between them.
If "Respond When: Form Is Submitted choosen" the flow has to be transparent and the user should be able to call as many Wait nodes as he want
